title: Batch jitter correlation lab notes — hypothesis handoff
content:
Attendees: Aisha Kumar (owner), Liam Chen (benchmarks), Sofia Rodriguez (runtime), Marcus Lee (observability), + on-call (brief join).

Summary (tl;dr):
We ran a focused lab to correlate observed batching jitter with p95 token latency spikes during sustained mixed-load shadow runs. Reproducible window: ~600–1400s into a 30-minute run where p95 climbs from baseline ~220ms to 650–900ms for ~30–90s bursts. Root-hypotheses narrowed to two leads: (1) sampler-induced batch size oscillation interacting with the sequencer queue and (2) transient KV-cache pressure + GC-like memory reclamation on older host types.

Experiment setup (short):
- Code baseline: bench harness v2.1.3 (branch: bench/mini-sampler).
- Runtime: serving-runtime image 2026-06-15 (kernel selector v0.9.2).
- Hardware: H100-like profile nodes (pool-A) and a small set of older A100 nodes (pool-B) to mimic fleet heterogeneity.
- Workload: mixed-seq synthetic generator; 25% long (1024 tokens), 50% medium (256), 25% short (32). QPS stepped from 200 → 650 over first 10m.
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), batch size distribution, sequencer queue depth, KV-cache hit/miss, host memory pressure, GC/OS reclaim events, scheduler latencies. Traces captured via distributed tracing and perf counters.

Baseline numbers (stable period):
- p50: 34ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 485ms.
- Mean batch size: 6.2 tokens per request cycle, stdev: 1.1.
- KV-cache hit ratio: 93% (prefix cache), cold miss rate ~7%.

Anomaly observed:
- Between t=600–1400s repeated spikes to p95=650–900ms lasting 20–120s.
- During spikes: sudden drop in mean batch size to ~2.1 followed by a recovery overshoot to ~9–12, then oscillation for ~30s. Sequencer queue depth showed sawtooth pattern indicating micro-scheduling delays.
- KV-cache observed transient miss-rate jumps to 25–40% coincident with batch oscillation windows on pool-B (A100 hosts). pool-A remained mostly steady.

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1 — Sampler/Batching feedback loop: the sampler's moving-window estimator reduces batch targets aggressively when it sees an increased tail (it reacted to early micro-latency leading to smaller batches, which reduces throughput and forces backlog, then sampler increases batch size, overshooting and causing new tail spikes). This negative-feedback loop explains sawtooth and correlates with p95 spikes.
H2 — KV-cache degradation on older hosts: pool-B shows transient memory pressure leading to increased cache evictions; cache misses force longer model compute paths or kernel fallbacks which spike latency. Could be exacerbated by lower NIC/network jitter on older instance type.
H3 — OS-level reclaim (rare): some hosts showed brief kernel reclaim events; less likely but not ruled out.

Evidence supporting H1:
- Batch size oscillator aligned with p95 spikes (correlation coefficient ~0.78 over window).
- Traces show increased sequencer latency (~12–30ms extra) when mean batch size is in low band.
- Re-running with sampler disabled (fixed batch target 6) removed the sawtooth and reduced spike magnitude by ~65% in a 15m test.

Evidence supporting H2:
- pool-B exhibits KV-cache miss bursts during spike windows. Memory RSS on these hosts briefly increases by ~8–12% before miss burst.
- Restarting one pool-B host (simulated) removed miss bursts for that node, but cluster-wide oscillation persisted if sampler active.

Quick reproducibility steps (dev run):
1) start bench harness v2.1.3 on pool-A + pool-B with mixed-seq config (same proportions).
2) enable full tracing and set sampler to adaptive (default). Wait for 30m run and inspect p95 windows at t=10m mark.
3) flip sampler to fixed-batch 6 and re-run; compare p95/p99 and batch distribution.
4) restart a sample pool-B node to observe KV-cache behaviour.

Immediate actions (agreed during sync):
- Short-term mitigation: roll-out a conservative sampler config (min_batch=4, max_increment_per_minute=1) to shadow fleet for next 48h to reduce oscillation amplitude. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2026-06-30.
- Follow-up lab: run targeted experiments isolating sampler from cache effects by: (a) fixed sampler + simulate cache evictions; (b) adaptive sampler + pin high cache hit on pool-B via priming. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 2026-07-02.
- Observability: add a derived metric `batch_oscillation_index` (stddev of batch size / mean batch size over 30s window) to perf dashboards and alert if >0.6. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-07-05.
- Infra: schedule a pool-B host kernel/AMI audit; check NIC driver versions and memory reclaim knobs. Owner: infra-team (linked ticket). ETA: 2026-07-07.

Longer term ideas (brainstormed):
- Sampler redesign: move from aggressive reactive estimator to a PID-style controller with explicit damping and sequencer-sourced backpressure signal. Put into bench A/B and evaluate.
- KV-cache hygiene: background prefetch/priming on long-tail sequences to reduce cold bursts; better eviction policy for pooled instances.
- Canary policy: when spike > X and batch_oscillation_index high, gracefully freeze sampler adjustments and fallback to conservative defaults.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why pool-A not affected by KV miss bursts? Differences in model kernel selection or allocator behavior? Need per-host binary comparison.
- Are there network micro-outages causing bursts concentrated on pool-B? Need NIC counters.
- Could an unrelated periodic job (cron/maintenance) be colliding? Check scheduled tasks.

Immediate blockers:
- We need infra permission to restart shadow hosts for more disruptive tests (Marcus is on it).
- Bench harness needs a small change to emit per-request batch-size label to traces (PR 789 is the change; awaiting review).

Action items (summary):
- Liam: conservative sampler roll-out to shadow (ETA 2026-06-30).
- Sofia: lab: fixed-sampler vs adaptive-sampler runs + cache-priming (ETA 2026-07-02).
- Marcus: dashboard metric + NIC/kernel audit kickoff (ETA 2026-07-05 / 2026-07-07).
- Aisha: consolidate results and write short postmortem if spike recurring after mitigations (ETA 2026-07-09).

Notes to self (informal):
- Sampler tuning is low-risk and buys us time; prioritize observability so we can quantify impact.
- Keep an eye on p99 trend even if p95 improves — microbursts can hide in tails.

Appendix: quick links and commands used during lab:
- Repro command (bench harness): `./bench/run --config mixed-seq.yaml --duration 00:30:00 --trace-level=full`
- Compare traces: `scripts/trace-compare --span batch_size --window 30s`
- PR for batch labels: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Jira: INF-2345 (batch jitter investigation)

Next sync: 2026-07-01 10:00 PST (short standup to review initial shadow rollout metrics).
